units.title: Unit 1 – Foundations of Big Data &
units.topics: Distributed Systems (06 Hours) Introduction to Big Data, Characteristics of Big Data, Traditional Data Processing vs Big Data Processing, Big Data Architecture, Data sources, Big Data ecosystems:parallel processing, data partitioning, data ingestion and storage mechanisms, Overview of distributed file systems, system architectures (client – server, peer -to-peer, cluster computing), Hadoop Distributed File System and processing frameworks: Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark. Case Study: A college generates large amounts of data such as attendance, exam results, LMS logs, and feedback forms/ Big Data Analytics in Smart City Traffic Management The traditional database system becomes slow during result processing. How can Big Data concepts help in handling Volume, Velocity, and Variety of campus data?

units.title: Distributed Storage & Resource Management
units.topics: Distributed File Systems: HDFS Architecture, NameNodes, DataNodes, Read/Write anatomy, Block replication. Cloud Object Storage: Introduction to AWS S3, Azure Blob, or Google Cloud Storage. Comparison with HDFS Distributed Data Storage Formats, Document -oriented: MongoDB, Column -family: Cassandra, Hbase Data Serialization: Efficient storage formats like Apache Parquet, Avro, and ORC. Hadoop YARN: Architecture (Resource Manager, Node Manager), Schedulers (FIFO, Capacity, Fair). Container Orchestration: Introduction to Kubernetes for data workloads (conceptual). Case Study: Cloud-Based Distributed Storage for Video Streaming Platform

units.title: Big Data Processing Frameworks
units.topics: Introduction to Big Data Processing - Need for distributed processing, Limitations of traditional RDBMS systems Batch processing vs Stream processing. Hadoop Ecosystem- Hadoop architecture, Hadoop core components such as HDFS (Hadoop Distributed File System), MapReduce Hadoop cluster architecture, MapReduce Programming Model, Introduction to Apache Spark, Spark Architecture – Driver, Executor, Cluster Manager, Resilient Distributed Datasets (RDD), RDD Operations – Transformations and Actions, DataFrames, Spark SQL, Spark Streaming basics. Case Study: Big Data Processing in E-Commerce – “ShopKart”

units.title: Streaming, Messaging & Real-Time Analytics
units.topics: Real-time data systems using Event -Driven Architecture (EDA): events, producers, consumers, brokers, and processing semantics, Lambda and Kappa architectures. Distributed messaging systems: publish –subscribe model, message queues, and log -based messaging, highlighting the architecture and components of Apache Kafka. Stream processing frameworks: micro-batching and Overview of real-time streaming using Apache Spark and Apache Flink, windowing techniques, event time vs processing time, watermarks, late data handling, and stateful vs. stateless processing. Real-time analytics applications: fraud detection, IoT analytics, and clickstream analysis. Case Study: Real-Time Fraud Detection in Banking Transactions- A bank wants to detect fraudulent transactions in real time and analyze customer spending behavior. How can Big Data analytics techniques help in prediction, fraud detection, and decision-making?

units.title: Data Governance, Security & Advanced Analytics
units.topics: Integration (06 Hours) Data governance: data quality, stewardship, ownership, master data management, metadata management, data lifecycle management, regulatory compliance (GDPR and HIPAA overview), and data lineage and auditing. Privacy concepts: Anonymization, pseudonymization, data masking, ethical issues, and governance standards. Advanced analytics: Batch analytics, use of Apache Spark MLlib, AI framework integration, data pipelines, model deployment and monitoring in big data systems. Case Study: Healthcare Big Data Governance and Security

Telecommunication Systems
units.topics: , Prerequisite Courses: Operating Systems, Computer Networks & Security Companion Course: Mobile Computing Lab Course Objectives: The course aims to: 1. To understand the fundamental concepts of mobile computing and wireless transmission. 2. To study various telecommunication systems like GSM and modern cellular standards. 3. To analyse mobile network and transport layer protocols for seamless connectivity. 4. To explore mobile databases, data dissemination, and synchronisation techniques. 5. To introduce mobile application development frameworks and security challenges. Course Outcomes: Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: • CO1: Explain the evolution and architecture of mobile computing and wireless transmission. • CO2: Compare various telecommunication systems including GSM, GPRS, and 5G. • CO3: Analyze mobile IP and transport layer variations for mobile environments. • CO4: Design data management and dissemination strategies for mobile databases. • CO5: Develop basic mobile applications using modern frameworks and secure them against threats. , , z Course Contents r Concepts: Evolution of Mobile Computing, History, Middleware and Gateways, Mob...

units.title: Mobile App Development & Security
units.topics: Mobile IP: IP Packet Delivery, Agent Discovery, Registration, Tunneling and Encapsulation, Opti- mization, Reverse Tunneling, IPv6 in Mobile Networks. Mobile TCP: Traditional TCP vs. Mobile TCP, Indirect TCP, Snooping TCP, Fast Retransmit/Fast Recovery, MPTCP (Multipath TCP). Ad-Hoc Networks: MANET routing protocols – DSDV (Proactive), DSR and AODV (Reactive), ZRP (Hybrid), Multicast routing (ODMRP). Vehicular Networks: VANET vs MANET, security issues in Ad-Hoc networks. Case Study: Design a mobile IP registration flow for a device moving across different subnets. Wireless Application Protocols: File system consistency, HTTP and HTML adaptations for wireless, WAP architecture (WDP, WTLS, WTP, WSP, WAE), WML, WML Script. Mobile Databases: Data Prefetching and Staging, Caching invalidation mechanisms, Client-server computing with adaptation, Power-aware data management. AI Integration at the Edge: Edge AI Inference for predictive prefetching, Lightweight Machine Learning models for user behaviour analysis, On-device model adaptation. Case Study: Study of Data Synchronization in mobile healthcare apps. Frameworks: Android and iOS Architectures, Native vs. Hybrid vs. Progressive Web...
